title: He didn’t call the polished.
paragraphs:
Jesus walked past the religious résumé.
Past the clean image.
Past the people who looked holy on the outside.

And He stopped for Levi — a tax collector.
A man with a dirty name, a compromised life, and a table full of sinners.
Then Jesus said two words that still shake the soul:

Not after you clean yourself.
Not after you fix your habits.
Not after you become “church-worthy.”

But here’s what we miss: Jesus is not attracted to sin.
He is moved by mercy.
He calls sinners out of darkness, not deeper into it.
“I came not to call the righteous, but sinners.” (Mark 2:17)

That line comforts the ashamed.
And confronts the proud.

Because the doorway to grace is not pretending you’re righteous.
It’s admitting you’re not.

If you feel disqualified, hidden, stained by your past — listen to me, kapatid:
You are exactly the kind of person Jesus calls.

Repent.
Rise.
Leave the old table.
Follow the Savior who still eats with sinners and transforms them into saints.

This is the Gospel:
We were not rescued because we were good.
We were rescued because Christ is merciful.
